prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
There’s no single service that guarantees visibility in LLMs like ChatGPT, but the best practical approach is to (1) make sure your business is listed in the authoritative local sources that LLMs use (Google Business Profile, Apple/Maps, Bing, Yelp, major directories) and (2) monitor those listings with a local‑SEO/listing management tool such as BrightLocal or Yext. Then directly test LLMs (ChatGPT, Bing Chat) by prompting them for local recommendations.

Why: LLMs don’t have a single public “business directory.” Their recommendations are driven by training data and by live knowledge sources (search engines, knowledge graphs, review sites) when browsing or retrieval is available. So being present and well‑documented in those sources is the reliable path to being recommended.

Recommended services/tools
- BrightLocal — excellent for local citation monitoring, review aggregation, rank tracking and simulating local search visibility.
- Yext — strong for pushing/managing listings across directories and monitoring how authoritative data sources show your business.
- Google Business Profile (free) — essential; check Insights and the Knowledge Panel.
- Bing Places / Apple Business Connect / Yelp — important sources LLMs may use.
- Semrush / Ahrefs / Moz — for tracking search presence and keyword visibility.
- Whitespark — citation building and local rank tracking.

How to test directly with ChatGPT and other LLMs
1. Ask the model directly: “Recommend a [type of business] in [city/neighborhood].” Try multiple phrasings and mention nearby landmarks.
2. Use the model’s browsing or plugins (if available) so it can fetch live info; otherwise remember offline models may be outdated.
3. Test multiple LLMs (ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Google Bard) — they pull from different sources.
4. Track whether your business appears over time as you improve listings.

Checklist to increase chance LLMs recommend you
- Claim and fully fill out your Google Business Profile (correct name, address, phone, hours, categories, photos).
- Claim Bing/Yelp/Apple and other major listings.
- Add structured data (schema.org LocalBusiness markup) to your website.
- Ensure consistent NAP (name, address, phone) across sites.
- Encourage genuine reviews on Google/Yelp and respond to them.
- Keep an authoritative “About” and location pages on your site with keywords and service area.
- Build local citations and quality backlinks.
- Use BrightLocal/Yext to monitor listings and fix inconsistencies.

Bottom line
If you want one place to start: use BrightLocal (or Yext if you prefer an enterprise push-and-manage solution) to audit and monitor your presence across the directories LLMs rely on, then actively test recommendations in ChatGPT/Bing/Google to confirm. Improving listings, structured data and reviews is the most reliable way to get LLMs to recommend your business.
